Original rubric

UI: Hierarchy, readability, spacing, visual consistency and responsive layout.

UX: Discoverability, keyboard access, scope retention, recovery and completion paths.

RA: Observable fit for research-administration tasks, evidence inspection, reuse and handoff. Not measured AI accuracy or demonstrated time savings.

SCALE: 9 exceptional; 8 strong with small friction; 7 useful with noticeable friction; 6 substantial learning or accessibility cost; 5 a serious limitation on the tested surface. Half-point grades are reviewer judgments, not precision measurements.

Verification and implementation

Frontend: 1,267 tests / 198 files passed. Typecheck and production build passed. Full lint: zero errors, 14 warnings; final changed-component lint: zero errors, one existing hook-dependency warning.

Final browser checks: 30 five-width file-to-Library states; 33 chat/source states including delayed initial scope; 42 actual 200% Chrome zoom states; 14 staff recovery states; nine actual local public-entry/first-module learning states. Earlier five-width 105 and enlarged-text 42 scans are indexed separately.

Backend: Actual isolated auth, team/project permissions, PDF storage/text extraction, atomic review/resume/export, workflow tuning persistence and manual/folder/schedule automation checks are separately recorded. Focused regression batches are listed in the implementation log; no model inference or external receiver success is inferred.

New findings closed: Duplicate invitation misuse, project-file role gaps, duplicate review decisions, repeated Apply/stale Revert, repeated automation events, mobile source/reply space, learning modal contrast/focus, initial draft-scope loss and citation-return races.

Remaining sessions: The acceptance guide and three fictional sources with 12 manually checked questions are ready. Actual screen-reader, model-backed labs/grounding and RA/specialist observations remain open.

Detailed item references and dated results are in the implementation log, 108-item checklist and route inventory. The portable evidence index distinguishes historical attempts, selected visual evidence and actual local backend checks.

Open work

  • R8-BASE-07 · P1 · Verify: Audit keyboard and assistive technology paths. Exercise row opening, card editing, menus, tabs, source links and recovery with the keyboard, then spot-check names, order and announcements with a screen reader. Automated scans do not close this item by themselves.
  • R8-CHAT-02 · P2 · Verify: Check grounding and evidence navigation. Use a manually checked set of sponsor/policy questions, including missing or conflicting information. Check deadline and budget claims against the cited passages; source inspection must preserve the conversation and reading position.
  • R8-AGENT-03 · P2 · Verify: Exercise actual tool lifecycle transitions. In isolated test execution, cover approval, cancellation, permission denial, interrupted streaming and retry. Confirm one accepted action produces one intended effect, including when the user refreshes or resends.
  • R8-VALIDATE-04 · P2 · Verify: Cover all three validation domains. Test KB, workflow and extraction validation with real-shaped cases, missing references, cancellation, refresh/resumption, history and apply/revert. Manually compare selected results with expected answers; fixture scores alone cannot close this item.
  • R8-LEARN-03 · P2 · Verify: Complete a representative learning path. Exercise lesson progress, assessment feedback, interruption/resumption, module unlock and course completion states. Check keyboard, mobile, short viewports and saved progress using controlled test accounts.
  • R8-GATE-03 · P2 · Verify: Check real execution separately from fixtures. Run representative flows against an isolated backend and controlled accounts, with non-delivering external-service stubs where needed. Record ingestion, persistence, worker/retry behavior, permission enforcement and model-answer spot checks separately from visual evidence.
  • R8-GATE-04 · P2 · Verify: Validate RA usefulness with representative users. Use a proposed acceptance study of at least five representative RAs performing five tasks: find a deadline, check a budget requirement, verify an extracted value, run a reusable review, and hand off a result. At least four of five users should complete each task unaided, with no unnoticed wrong-source or unintended-approval error. Record time, errors, evidence checks and handoff usability; this is a formative gate, not a statistical guarantee.
  • R8-GATE-05 · P2 · Verify: Validate specialist task fit with the right roles. Observe a team owner investigating a failed run, an integration maintainer repairing a connection, an examiner reviewing a submission and support staff responding to a ticket. Ordinary RAs must also be able to identify when they need these roles and where to request help.

Limits and deployment state

  • Actual screen-reader use, five-RA acceptance study and specialist observations have not occurred.
  • Real chat grounding, agent actions, model-backed validation and the full learning course need a configured development model connection.
  • Most browser evidence uses explicit synthetic API fixtures. Live local backend evidence is separately identified and uses synthetic accounts/data.
  • Actual local task bodies were exercised with isolated Mongo/Redis and file/SMTP sinks; no production data, broker consumer or external-service delivery was used.

Selected screenshots are embedded in this file and survive raw QA cleanup. Source scripts remain reproducible. No user-study observations or model answers were invented. The report is not a production-release sign-off.
